Gujarat Subah.fact: Bahadur Shah continued to pursue the retreating forces defeating them in battle at Kanij near Mahemdavad.

Taking advantage of the absence of the Gáikwár and his army in the Dakhan, Jawán Mard Khán marched into Sorath.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: He first visited Ghogha, and then levying tribute in Gohilwad advanced into Kathiawad and marched against Nawanagar, and, after collecting a contribution from the Jám, returned to Áhmedábád.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Bálájiráv agreed, and from that time an agent of the _____ was established at Cambay
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: In 1752, as soon as the news reached Gujarát that the Maráthás’ share in the province had been divided between the Peshwa and Gáikwár, Momín Khán, who was always quarrelling with the Gáikwár's agent, sending Varajlál his steward to Bálájiráv Peshwa begged him to include Cambay in his share and send his agent in place of the Gáikwár's agent. Bálájiráv agreed, and from that time an agent of the Peshwa was set up at Cambay.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: In the same year _____áthráv, brother of the Peshwa, entering Gujarát took possession of the Rewa and Mahi Kántha districts and marched on Surat
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: In the same year Raghunáthráv, brother of the Peshwa, entering Gujarát took possession of the Rewa and Mahi Kántha districts and marched on Surat.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Shiaji Dhangar was appointed in _____ám's place as Dámáji's deputy, and Krishnáji came to collect the Peshwa's share
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Shiaji Dhangar was appointed in Shevakrám's place as Dámáji's deputy, and Krishnáji came to collect the Peshwa's share.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Bharuch Independent, _____ Up to this time the city of Bharuch had remained part of the Nizám's personal estate, managed by Abdúllah Beg, whom, with the title of Nek Álam Khán, Ásif Jáh the late Nizám
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Bharuch Independent, 1752 Up to this time the city of Bharuch had remained part of the Nizám's personal estate, managed by Abdúllah Beg, whom, with the title of Nek Álam Khán, Ásif Jáh the late Nizám-ul-Mulk had chosen his deputy. On the death of Abdúllah Beg in 1752 the emperor appointed his son to succeed him with the same title as his father, while he gave to another son, named Mughal Beg, the title of Khertalab Khán.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Pándurang Pandit Repulsed at Áhmedábád, 1752 The Peshwa now sent Pándurang Pandit to levy tribute from his share of Gujarát, and that officer crossing the Mahi marched upon Cambay. Momín Khán prepared to oppose him, but the Pandit made friendly overtures, and eventually Momín Khán not only paid the sum of Rupees 7000 for grass and grain for the Pandit's troops, but also lent him four small cannon.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: During the siege Pándurang _____, sending some troops, ravaged Nikol, part of the lands of Áli Muhammad Khán Bahádur, the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Pándurang Pandit Repulsed at Áhmedábád, 1752 The Peshwa now sent Pándurang Pandit to levy tribute from his share of Gujarát, and that officer crossing the Mahi marched upon Cambay. Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Meanwhile, as the operations against Áhmedábád made no progress, Pándurang _____ made offers of peace
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Momín Khán prepared to oppose him, but the Pandit made friendly overtures, and eventually Momín Khán not only paid the sum of Rupees 7000 for grass and grain for the Pandit's troops, but also lent him four small cannon. Pándurang Pandit then marched upon Áhmedábád, and encamping near the Kankaria Lake laid siege to the city which was defended by Jawán Mard Khán.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: About this time the _____ released Dámáji Gáikwár on his promise to help the Peshwa's brother Raghunáthráv, who was shortly afterwards despatched with an army to complete the conquest of Gujarát
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: About this time the Peshwa released Dámáji Gáikwár on his promise to help the Peshwa's brother Raghunáthráv, who was shortly afterwards despatched with an army to complete the conquest of Gujarát.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Meanwhile, Jawán _____án's anxiety regarding the Maráthás was for a time removed by the departure of Pándurang Pandit
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: These Jawán Mard Khán accepted, and on receiving from Jawán Mard Khán the present of a mare and a small sum of money under the name of entertainment, the Marátha leader withdrew to Sorath. Meanwhile, Jawán Mard Khán's anxiety regarding the Maráthás was for a time removed by the departure of Pándurang Pandit.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Jawán _____án then marched from the city, levying tribute until he arrived on the Pálanpur frontier about seventy-five miles north of Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Certain well informed persons, who had heard of Raghunáthráv's preparations for invading Gujarát, begged Jawán Mard Khán not to leave the city but to depute his brother Zoráwar Khán Bábi to collect the tribute. Jawán Mard Khán, not believing their reports, said that he would not go more than from forty-five to sixty miles from the city, and that, should the necessity of any more distant excursion arise, he would entrust it to his brother.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Here meeting Muhammad Bahádur Jhálori, the governor of Palanpur, Jawán Mard Khán was foolishly induced to join him in plundering the fertile districts of Sirohi, till at last he was not less than ____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Here meeting Muhammad Bahádur Jhálori, the governor of Palanpur, Jawán Mard Khán was foolishly induced to join him in plundering the fertile districts of Sirohi, till at last he was not less than 150 miles from his headquarters.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Meanwhile, _____áthráv, joining Dámáji Gáikwár, entered suddenly by an unusual route into Gujarát, and news reached Áhmedábád that the Maráthás had crossed the Narmada River
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Meanwhile, Raghunáthráv, joining Dámáji Gáikwár, entered suddenly by an unusual route into Gujarát, and news reached Áhmedábád that the Maráthás had crossed the Narmada River. Raghunáthráv, hearing that Jawán Mard Khán and his army were absent from the city, pressed on by forced marches, and crossing the Mahi River despatched an advance co.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Kosáji, proprietor of _____, at Dámáji Gáikwár's invitation also marched towards Áhmedábád, plundering Mehmúdábád Khokhri, only three miles from the city
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Kosáji, proprietor of Nadiad, at Dámáji Gáikwár's invitation also marched towards Áhmedábád, plundering Mehmúdábád Khokhri, only three miles from the city.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: In the meantime _____ reached Kaira (Kheda), and taking with him the chief man of that place, Muhammad Daurán, son of Muhammad Bábi, continued his march
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Raghunáthráv, hearing that Jawán Mard Khán and his army were absent from the city, pressed on by forced marches, and crossing the Mahi River despatched an advance corps under Vithal Sukhdev. In the meantime Vithal Sukhdev reached Kaira (Kheda), and taking with him the chief man of that place, Muhammad Daurán, son of Muhammad Bábi, continued his march.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: He was shortly joined by _____áthráv, and the combined forces now proceeded to Áhmedábád and encamped by the Kánkaria lake
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Raghunáthráv, hearing that Jawán Mard Khán and his army were absent from the city, pressed on by forced marches, and crossing the Mahi River despatched an advance corps under Vithal Sukhdev. He was shortly joined by Raghunáthráv, and the combined forces now proceeded to Áhmedábád and encamped by the Kánkaria lake.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Next day _____áthráv moved his camp to near the tomb of Sháh Bhíkan, on the bank of the Sabarmati River to the south-west of the city
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: He was shortly joined by Raghunáthráv, and the combined forces now proceeded to Áhmedábád and encamped by the Kánkaria lake. Next day Raghunáthráv moved his camp to near the tomb of Sháh Bhíkan, on the bank of the Sabarmati River to the south-west of the city.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: After leaving Sirohi, Jawán _____án had gone westwards to Tharad and Vav, so that the first messengers failed to find him
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: After leaving Sirohi, Jawán Mard Khán had gone westwards to Tharad and Vav, so that the first messengers failed to find him. One of the later messengers, Mándan by name, who had not left Áhmedábád until the arrival of Raghunáthráv at the Kánkaria lake, made his way to Váv and Tharád, and told Jawán Mard Khán what had happened.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: The presence of Jawán _____án raised the spirits of the besieged, and the defence was conducted with ardour
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: After leaving Sirohi, Jawán Mard Khán had gone westwards to Tharad and Vav, so that the first messengers failed to find him. One of the later messengers, Mándan by name, who had not left Áhmedábád until the arrival of Raghunáthráv at the Kánkaria lake, made his way to Váv and Tharád, and told Jawán Mard Khán what had happened.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At length, embarrassed by want of provisions and the clamour of his troops for pay, he extorted _____ 50,000 from the official classes
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: At length, embarrassed by want of provisions and the clamour of his troops for pay, he extorted Rupees 50,000 from the official classes.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At last to _____áthráv's relief, Jawán Mard Khán was reduced to treat for peace through Vithal Sukhdev
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: The official classes who were the repository of all real power murmured against his rule and openly advocated the surrender of the city, and Jawán Mard Khán, much against his will, was forced to enter into negotiations with Raghunáthráv. Raghunáthráv was so little hopeful of taking Áhmedábád that he had determined, should the siege last a month longer, to depart on condition of receiving the one-fourth share of the revenue and a safe conduct.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: It was arranged that the Maráthás should give Jawán _____án the sum of Rupees 1 lákh to pay his troops, besides presenting him with an elephant and other articles of value
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Had Jawán Mard Khán only disbursed his own money to pay the troops, and encouraged instead of disheartening the official class, he need never have lost the city. At last to Raghunáthráv's relief, Jawán Mard Khán was reduced to treat for peace through Vithal Sukhdev.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: It was further agreed that one of Jawán _____án's brothers should always serve the Maráthás with 300 horse and 500 foot, the expenses of the force being paid by the Maráthás
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: It was arranged that the Maráthás should give Jawán Mard Khán the sum of Rupees 1 lákh to pay his troops, besides presenting him with an elephant and other articles of value. And that, for himself and his brothers, Jawán Mard Khán should receive, free from any Marátha claim, the districts of Patan, Vadnagar, Sami, Munjpur, Visnagar, Tharád, Kheralu, and Rádhanpur with Tervada and Vijapur.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: The treaty was then delivered to Jawán Mard Khán, and he and his garrison, marching out with the honours of war, the Maráthás took possession of Áhmedábád on 2 April _____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: The treaty was then delivered to Jawán Mard Khán, and he and his garrison, marching out with the honours of war, the Maráthás took possession of Áhmedábád on 2 April 1753.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: On leaving Áhmedábád Jawán _____án retired to Pátan
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: The treaty was then delivered to Jawán Mard Khán, and he and his garrison, marching out with the honours of war, the Maráthás took possession of Áhmedábád on 2 April 1753. On leaving Áhmedábád Jawán Mard Khán retired to Pátan.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At Áhmedábád _____áthráv with Dámáji arranged for the government of the city, appointing Shripatráv his deputy
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: This agreement was signed and sealed by Raghunáthráv, with Dámáji Gáikwár (half sharer), Malhárráv Holkar, Jye Ápa Sindhia, Rámchandar Vithal Sukhdev, Sakhárám Bhagvant, and Mádhavráv Gopálráv as securities. At Áhmedábád Raghunáthráv with Dámáji arranged for the government of the city, appointing Shripatráv his deputy.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: He then marched into _____ to levy tribute from the Limbdi and Wadhwan chiefs; and was so far successful that Harbhamji of Limbḍi agreed to pay an annual tribute of Rupees 40,000
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: He then marched into Jhalawad to levy tribute from the Limbdi and Wadhwan chiefs; and was so far successful that Harbhamji of Limbḍi agreed to pay an annual tribute of Rupees 40,000.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: As the rainy season was drawing near Raghunáthráv returned to Dholka, while _____ forced Muhammad Bahádur, the governor of Palanpur, to consent to a payment of Rupees 1,15,000
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: As the rainy season was drawing near Raghunáthráv returned to Dholka, while Patel Vithal Sukhdev forced Muhammad Bahádur, the governor of Palanpur, to consent to a payment of Rupees 1,15,000.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: From Dholka, _____áthráv went to Tárápur, about twelve miles north of Cambay (Khambhat), and compelled Momín Khán to submit to an annual payment of Rupees 10,000
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: At Áhmedábád Raghunáthráv with Dámáji arranged for the government of the city, appointing Shripatráv his deputy. As the rainy season was drawing near Raghunáthráv returned to Dholka, while Patel Vithal Sukhdev forced Muhammad Bahádur, the governor of Palanpur, to consent to a payment of Rupees 1,15,000.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As the viceroy was in need of money, he farmed to one Jívan Jugal the districts of _____, Makbúlábad or Amod about twenty-two miles north of Bharuch, Dholka, and Bharuch
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: As the viceroy was in need of money, he farmed to one Jívan Jugal the districts of Jambusar, Makbúlábad or Amod about twenty-two miles north of Bharuch, Dholka, and Bharuch.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____, he came to Áhmedábád with Áli Muhammad Khán father of the author of the Mirát-i-Áhmedi, as his private minister
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1724, he came to Áhmedábád with Áli Muhammad Khán father of the author of the Mirát-i-Áhmedi, as his private minister.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The emperor accepted this offer, allowing _____ Áli to draw on the Surat treasury to the extent of Rupees 200000
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Rustam Áli, governor of Surat, having succeeded twice or thrice in defeating the Maráthás under Píláji Gáikwár, now offered, in conjunction with his brother Shujáât Khán, that if 20,000 men were placed under their orders, they would march against the Nizám. The emperor accepted this offer, allowing Rustam Áli to draw on the Surat treasury to the extent of Rupees 200000.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He promised to Kántáji _____ Bánde a one-fourth share of the revenue of Gujarát, provided he should be able, in concert with Hámid Khán, to re-conquer the province from Mubáriz-ul-Mulk
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He promised to Kántáji Kadam Bánde a one-fourth share of the revenue of Gujarát, provided he should be able, in concert with Hámid Khán, to re-conquer the province from Mubáriz-ul-Mulk. Hámid Khán seeing his opportunity, united his forces with those of Kántáji Kadam, and marched to Kapadvanj.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shujáât Khán, who was now at Kadi, instead of following the advice of his minister and carefully watching Hámid Khán's movements from _____, went to a distant part of the province
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán, who was now at Kadi, instead of following the advice of his minister and carefully watching Hámid Khán's movements from Kapadvanj, went to a distant part of the province. Hámid Khán seeing his opportunity, united his forces with those of Kántáji Kadam, and marched to Kapadvanj.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán seeing his opportunity, united his forces with those of Kántáji Kadam, and marched to _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán, who was now at Kadi, instead of following the advice of his minister and carefully watching Hámid Khán's movements from Kapadvanj, went to a distant part of the province. Hámid Khán seeing his opportunity, united his forces with those of Kántáji Kadam, and marched to Kapadvanj.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shujáât Khán hearing of this, advanced towards Áhmedábád and encamped at _____ near Áhmedábád and then proceeded to Mota Medra, about six miles east of the capital
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán hearing of this, advanced towards Áhmedábád and encamped at Dabhoda near Áhmedábád and then proceeded to Mota Medra, about six miles east of the capital.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán seeing that _____áât Khán had but a small force, marched between him and the capital
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán hearing of this, advanced towards Áhmedábád and encamped at Dabhoda near Áhmedábád and then proceeded to Mota Medra, about six miles east of the capital. Hámid Khán seeing that Shujáât Khán had but a small force, marched between him and the capital.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: A battle was fought, in which Shujáât Khán was slain, and his two sons Hasan Kúli and _____ Kúli were taken prisoners
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: A battle was fought, in which Shujáât Khán was slain, and his two sons Hasan Kúli and Mustafa Kúli were taken prisoners.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shujáât Khán's head was cut off and sent to _____án Bábi, to be sent to Ibráhím Kúli his son, who was doing duty as commandant at Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán's head was cut off and sent to Safdar Khán Bábi, to be sent to Ibráhím Kúli his son, who was doing duty as commandant at Áhmedábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán now sent a message to the emperor, that the Maráthás had been successful in defeating _____áât Khán and conquering Gujarát, but that he had defended Áhmedábád against them
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: A battle was fought, in which Shujáât Khán was slain, and his two sons Hasan Kúli and Mustafa Kúli were taken prisoners. Shujáât Khán's head was cut off and sent to Safdar Khán Bábi, to be sent to Ibráhím Kúli his son, who was doing duty as commandant at Áhmedábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Kántáji went to _____ and besieged the town, but on the promise of one of the chief inhabitants to raise a sum of Rupees 350000, the Maráthás retired
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Kántáji went to Viramgam and besieged the town, but on the promise of one of the chief inhabitants to raise a sum of Rupees 350000, the Maráthás retired.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Ibráhím Kúli, son of _____áât Khán, in revenge for his father's death, determined to assassinate Hámid Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Ibráhím Kúli, son of Shujáât Khán, in revenge for his father's death, determined to assassinate Hámid Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Píláji promised to aid _____án, and the allied armies, crossing the Mahi River, encamped at Aras in the plain between Anand Anand and the Mahi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Píláji promised to aid Rustam Khán, and the allied armies, crossing the Mahi River, encamped at Aras in the plain between Anand Anand and the Mahi. Hámid Khán, accompanied by Mír Nathu, Muhammad Salábat Rohila, and Kántáji Kadam, marched to oppose Rustam Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán, accompanied by Mír Nathu, _____ábat Rohila, and Kántáji Kadam, marched to oppose Rustam Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Hámid Khán, accompanied by Mír Nathu, Muhammad Salábat Rohila, and Kántáji Kadam, marched to oppose Rustam Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: A battle was fought, in which, though Piláji took no part, Hámid Khán was defeated and put to flight, and Mír _____ was killed
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Hámid Khán, accompanied by Mír Nathu, Muhammad Salábat Rohila, and Kántáji Kadam, marched to oppose Rustam Khán. A battle was fought, in which, though Piláji took no part, Hámid Khán was defeated and put to flight, and Mír Nathu was killed.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: After the fight _____ Áli remained on the field of battle and liberated his nephews, plundering Hámid Khán's camp
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Hámid Khán, accompanied by Mír Nathu, Muhammad Salábat Rohila, and Kántáji Kadam, marched to oppose Rustam Khán. After the fight Rustam Áli remained on the field of battle and liberated his nephews, plundering Hámid Khán's camp.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Píláji plundered _____ Áli's camp and then moved off, while Kántáji carried away what was left in the camp of Hámid Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: After the fight Rustam Áli remained on the field of battle and liberated his nephews, plundering Hámid Khán's camp. Píláji plundered Rustam Áli's camp and then moved off, while Kántáji carried away what was left in the camp of Hámid Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Now, as the Maráthás really desired to ruin _____ Áli, who was their bitter foe, they after a few days surrounded him and cut off his supplies
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: After the fight Rustam Áli remained on the field of battle and liberated his nephews, plundering Hámid Khán's camp. Píláji plundered Rustam Áli's camp and then moved off, while Kántáji carried away what was left in the camp of Hámid Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán reproached Kántáji for his inactivity; but he pleaded in excuse that he was watching the mode of warfare amongst _____, and promised to attack Rustam Áli shortly
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Hámid Khán reproached Kántáji for his inactivity; but he pleaded in excuse that he was watching the mode of warfare amongst Mughals, and promised to attack Rustam Áli shortly.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He extorted large sums from the rich, and poisoned the two sons of _____áât Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He extorted large sums from the rich, and poisoned the two sons of Shujáât Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: When the news of Kántáji's and Píláji's success reached the Dakhan, _____, son of Khanderáv Senápati, came with a large army and laid siege to Cambay
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When the news of Kántáji's and Píláji's success reached the Dakhan, Trimbak Rao Dabhade, son of Khanderáv Senápati, came with a large army and laid siege to Cambay.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk recaptures the province from Hamid Khan and the Maráthás, _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk recaptures the province from Hamid Khan and the Maráthás, 1725.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Salábat Khán, leaving Áhmedábád, went to Víramgám, and after some time, placing his nephew at Víramgám, he went into _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Salábat Khán, leaving Áhmedábád, went to Víramgám, and after some time, placing his nephew at Víramgám, he went into Gohilwad.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: When the news of the defeat and death of _____ Áli reached Delhi, the emperor ordered Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to take a strong army and proceed in person to Gujarát and expel Hámid Khán and the Maráthás
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When the news of the defeat and death of Rustam Áli reached Delhi, the emperor ordered Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to take a strong army and proceed in person to Gujarát and expel Hámid Khán and the Maráthás.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk marched on Gujarát with a large army, assisted by Mahárája _____ of Jodhpur, Chatarsingh Rája of Narwar in Bundelkhand, Gandrapsingh, and the Mahárána of Udaipur
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk marched on Gujarát with a large army, assisted by Mahárája Abheysingh of Jodhpur, Chatarsingh Rája of Narwar in Bundelkhand, Gandrapsingh, and the Mahárána of Udaipur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At that time Salábat Khán was removed from his government, and _____án Bábi died
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: At that time Salábat Khán was removed from his government, and Safdar Khán Bábi died.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In obedience to the imperial order, Mubáriz-ul-_____ marched from Ajmer and came to the Gujarát frontier
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk marched on Gujarát with a large army, assisted by Mahárája Abheysingh of Jodhpur, Chatarsingh Rája of Narwar in Bundelkhand, Gandrapsingh, and the Mahárána of Udaipur. On his arrival at Ajmer, Mubáriz-ul-Mulk was received by his private minister Áli Muhammad Khán, who afterwards joined Jawán Mard Khán Bábi in Rádhanpur, and united their troops with those under Mubáriz-ul-Mulk.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He placed Rúpsingh and Sardár _____ in charge of the city and himself withdrew to Mehmúdábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He placed Rúpsingh and Sardár Muhammad Ghorni in charge of the city and himself withdrew to Mehmúdábád. When Sheikh Alíyár arrived before the city, Muhammad Ghorni, who was dissatisfied with Hámid Khán for bringing in the Maráthás, persuaded Rúpsingh to fly.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk now sent _____íyár in advance with an army against Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk now sent Sheikh Alíyár in advance with an army against Áhmedábád. When Sheikh Alíyár arrived before the city, Muhammad Ghorni, who was dissatisfied with Hámid Khán for bringing in the Maráthás, persuaded Rúpsingh to fly.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In the meantime Mubáriz-ul-Mulk with the main body of his forces reached _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the meantime Mubáriz-ul-Mulk with the main body of his forces reached Sidhpur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán, accompanied by a detachment of Marátha horse, now returned to Áhmedábád; but _____ closed the gates, and would not suffer him to enter the city
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When Sheikh Alíyár arrived before the city, Muhammad Ghorni, who was dissatisfied with Hámid Khán for bringing in the Maráthás, persuaded Rúpsingh to fly. Hámid Khán, accompanied by a detachment of Marátha horse, now returned to Áhmedábád; but Muhammad Ghorni closed the gates, and would not suffer him to enter the city.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk marched to _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk marched to Mehsana.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time Áli _____án, the father of the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi, who was now with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk at Mehsána, advised him to conciliate the influential family of Bábi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Áli Muhammad Khán, the father of the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi, who was now with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk at Mehsána, advised him to conciliate the influential family of Bábi. Under his advice, Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi was appointed governor of Víramgám, and Jawán Mard Khán governor of Pátan.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Under his advice, Salábat _____án Bábi was appointed governor of Víramgám, and Jawán Mard Khán governor of Pátan
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Áli Muhammad Khán, the father of the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi, who was now with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk at Mehsána, advised him to conciliate the influential family of Bábi. Under his advice, Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi was appointed governor of Víramgám, and Jawán Mard Khán governor of Pátan.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time Áli _____án was dismissed from the post of minister, and in his stead first Muhammad Sayad Beg and afterwards Muhammad Sulaimán were appointed
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Áli Muhammad Khán, the father of the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi, who was now with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk at Mehsána, advised him to conciliate the influential family of Bábi. Under his advice, Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi was appointed governor of Víramgám, and Jawán Mard Khán governor of Pátan.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shortly afterwards _____ás, the Gujaráti minister of Hámid Khán, deserted his master's declining cause
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shortly afterwards Murlidhardás, the Gujaráti minister of Hámid Khán, deserted his master's declining cause.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Before the close of _____, Mubáriz-ul-Mulk reached Áhmedábád, where he was well received by the officials and merchants
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Before the close of 1725, Mubáriz-ul-Mulk reached Áhmedábád, where he was well received by the officials and merchants.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán and _____áji, who had by this time reached the banks of the Mahi river, were now joined by Píláji Gáikwár
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When Kantáji heard that Mubáriz-ul-Mulk had arrived at Pethápur, only eighteen miles from Áhmedábád, he retired to Mehmúdábád. Hámid Khán and Kantáji, who had by this time reached the banks of the Mahi river, were now joined by Píláji Gáikwár.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk deputed his son Khánahzád Khán with an army to oppose them, and made several appointments, among other changes raising Áli _____án to the post of minister
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk deputed his son Khánahzád Khán with an army to oppose them, and made several appointments, among other changes raising Áli Muhammad Khán to the post of minister.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Defeat of the Maráthás at Sojitra and Kapadvanj, _____ Khánahzád Khán met the Maráthás near Sojitra, about ten miles north-west of Petlád, and defeated them, pursuing them as far as the Mahi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Defeat of the Maráthás at Sojitra and Kapadvanj, 1725 Khánahzád Khán met the Maráthás near Sojitra, about ten miles north-west of Petlád, and defeated them, pursuing them as far as the Mahi.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Then, returning, he was reinforced by his brother Sháh Nawáz Khán, and marched against the Maráthás, who were encamped at _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Defeat of the Maráthás at Sojitra and Kapadvanj, 1725 Khánahzád Khán met the Maráthás near Sojitra, about ten miles north-west of Petlád, and defeated them, pursuing them as far as the Mahi. Then, returning, he was reinforced by his brother Sháh Nawáz Khán, and marched against the Maráthás, who were encamped at Kapadvanj.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Another battle was fought, and the Maráthás were again defeated and pursued as far as the hills of Áli-Mohan now _____ in the extreme east of the province
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Another battle was fought, and the Maráthás were again defeated and pursued as far as the hills of Áli-Mohan now Chhota Udaipur in the extreme east of the province.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Khánahzád Khán now appointed Hasan-ud-dín governor of Baroda, _____, Jambusar, and Makbulábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Khánahzád Khán now appointed Hasan-ud-dín governor of Baroda, Bharuch, Jambusar, and Makbulábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The Nágars accordingly, seeing no prospect of help, paid a sum of _____ 400000 and Antáji Bháskar retired
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Nágars accordingly, seeing no prospect of help, paid a sum of Rupees 400000 and Antáji Bháskar retired.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Kántáji again laid siege to _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Vadnagar was inhabited by wealthy Bráhmans of the Nágar caste who prayed Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to march to their relief; but as both his sons were in pursuit of the other Marátha bands defeated at Kapadvanj, the viceroy had no troops to spare from the Áhmedábád garrison. Kántáji again laid siege to Vadnagar.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shortly afterwards _____ in the Kaira district suffered a similar fate at the hands of Kántáji
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shortly afterwards Umreth in the Kaira district suffered a similar fate at the hands of Kántáji.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In one of his raids Píláji Gáikwár advancing as far as _____ was met by Khánahzád Khán, the son of the viceroy
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In one of his raids Píláji Gáikwár advancing as far as Baroda was met by Khánahzád Khán, the son of the viceroy.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Distrusting the issue of a battle Píláji fled to _____, and from Cambay withdrew to Sorath
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Distrusting the issue of a battle Píláji fled to Cambay, and from Cambay withdrew to Sorath.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: For these services the emperor raised Khánahzád Khán to the rank of a noble, with the title Ghálib _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: For these services the emperor raised Khánahzád Khán to the rank of a noble, with the title Ghálib Jang.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Not long afterwards Áli _____án was again entrusted with a command and raised to be governor of Dholka
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Áli Muhammad Khán was dismissed from the post of minister, and in his stead first Muhammad Sayad Beg and afterwards Muhammad Sulaimán were appointed. Not long afterwards Áli Muhammad Khán was again entrusted with a command and raised to be governor of Dholka.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The Maráthás retired to the Dakhan, but, returning in _____, compelled Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to confirm his predecessor's grants in their favour
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Maráthás retired to the Dakhan, but, returning in 1726, compelled Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to confirm his predecessor's grants in their favour.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As part of the agreement between Mubáriz-ul-_____ and the Marátha chiefs Píláji was to receive a share in the revenue of the districts south of the Mahi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Maráthás retired to the Dakhan, but, returning in 1726, compelled Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to confirm his predecessor's grants in their favour. As part of the agreement between Mubáriz-ul-Mulk and the Marátha chiefs Píláji was to receive a share in the revenue of the districts south of the Mahi.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time want of funds forced Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to sell the greater part of the _____ district to different landholders
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time want of funds forced Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to sell the greater part of the Dholka district to different landholders.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Though he did not consent to these proposals, the viceroy so far accepted the alliance of the _____ as to allow the governor of Baroda to aid Udáji Pavár against Píláji
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Kántáji, perceiving that if the Peshwa became supreme his own independence would suffer, joined Píláji, and marching together upon Baroda they endeavoured, but without success, to prevent the Mughal governor Sadr-ud-dín Khán from entering the city. In the following year, 1727, Bájiráv Peshwa began to negotiate with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk, undertaking that if the one-fourth and one-tenth shares in the revenue of the province were guaranteed to him, he would protect Gujarát from other invaders.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Piláji Gáikwár obtains Baroda and Dabhoi, _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the following year, 1727, Bájiráv Peshwa began to negotiate with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk, undertaking that if the one-fourth and one-tenth shares in the revenue of the province were guaranteed to him, he would protect Gujarát from other invaders. Piláji Gáikwár obtains Baroda and Dabhoi, 1727.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Píláji Gáikwár now obtained possession of _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Though he did not consent to these proposals, the viceroy so far accepted the alliance of the Peshwa as to allow the governor of Baroda to aid Udáji Pavár against Píláji. Piláji Gáikwár obtains Baroda and Dabhoi, 1727.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk, still sorely pressed for funds, marched into _____ to exact tribute
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk, still sorely pressed for funds, marched into Sorath to exact tribute.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: On reaching Víramgám, Salábat _____án Bábi, on behalf of the Jám of Nawánagar, presented the viceroy with Rupees 100000, and for this service was rewarded with the gift of an elephant
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: On reaching Víramgám, Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, on behalf of the Jám of Nawánagar, presented the viceroy with Rupees 100000, and for this service was rewarded with the gift of an elephant.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk then marched against Chháya, the capital of the chief of _____ in the south-west of Káthiáwad
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk then marched against Chháya, the capital of the chief of Porbandar in the south-west of Káthiáwad.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: But on hearing that the viceroy proposed to annex his territory and appoint an officer to govern it, he returned and agreed to pay a tribute of _____ 40,000
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: On reaching Víramgám, Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, on behalf of the Jám of Nawánagar, presented the viceroy with Rupees 100000, and for this service was rewarded with the gift of an elephant. But on hearing that the viceroy proposed to annex his territory and appoint an officer to govern it, he returned and agreed to pay a tribute of Rupees 40,000.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time the viceroy received orders from the emperor to restore certain land which he had confiscated, and as he neglected to obey, certain estates of his in the _____áb were resumed
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time the viceroy received orders from the emperor to restore certain land which he had confiscated, and as he neglected to obey, certain estates of his in the Panjáb were resumed.

Nizám-ul-Mulk agreed, appointed Abdúlláh his deputy, and ennobled him with the title of Nek Álam Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About the same time _____, brother of the viceroy, withdrew to his chiefship of Nágor in Jodhpur, and Ázmat-ulláh went to Ágra
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About the same time Vakhatsingh, brother of the viceroy, withdrew to his chiefship of Nágor in Jodhpur, and Ázmat-ulláh went to Ágra.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Momín Khán received the farm of _____, and Kántáji was confirmed in the share he had acquired of the revenues of Gujarát
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Momín Khán received the farm of Petlad, and Kántáji was confirmed in the share he had acquired of the revenues of Gujarát.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____ the paymaster, Amánatdár Khán, died, and was succeeded by Ghulám Hasan Khán, who sent Mujáhid-ud-dín Khán to act as his deputy
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1732 the paymaster, Amánatdár Khán, died, and was succeeded by Ghulám Hasan Khán, who sent Mujáhid-ud-dín Khán to act as his deputy.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Through the influence of _____, Sohráb Áli was now confirmed as governor of Surat, and Mustafíd Khán was obliged to return to Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Through the influence of Mulla Muhammad Ali, Sohráb Áli was now confirmed as governor of Surat, and Mustafíd Khán was obliged to return to Áhmedábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The recent acquisition of the town of _____ and of the strong fortress of Dabhoi had made Piláji still more formidable
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The recent acquisition of the town of Baroda and of the strong fortress of Dabhoi had made Piláji still more formidable. Under these circumstances, Abheysingh, who had long wished to recover Baroda and Dabhoi determined to assassinate Piláji, and this was effected by a Márvádi at the village of Dakor.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: They then evacuated the district of _____, retiring to the fortress of Dabhoi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The recent acquisition of the town of Baroda and of the strong fortress of Dabhoi had made Piláji still more formidable. Under these circumstances, Abheysingh, who had long wished to recover Baroda and Dabhoi determined to assassinate Piláji, and this was effected by a Márvádi at the village of Dakor.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Under these circumstances, _____, who had long wished to recover Baroda and Dabhoi determined to assassinate Piláji, and this was effected by a Márvádi at the village of Dakor
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Píláji Gáikwár as the agent of the deceased Khanderáv Dábháde Senápati, as the owner of the fort of Songad, and as the ally of the Bhíls and Kolis, was naturally a thorn in the side of the viceroy Abheysingh. Under these circumstances, Abheysingh, who had long wished to recover Baroda and Dabhoi determined to assassinate Piláji, and this was effected by a Márvádi at the village of Dakor.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: On hearing of the death of Píláji, the viceroy immediately advanced against the Maráthás, and, after taking possession of _____, laid siege to Dabhoi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Under these circumstances, Abheysingh, who had long wished to recover Baroda and Dabhoi determined to assassinate Piláji, and this was effected by a Márvádi at the village of Dakor. The Maráthás slew the assassin and withdrew across the Mahi, burning the body of Piláji at the village of Savli, fourteen miles north of Baroda.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He then went to _____, and after placing Sher Khán Bábi in charge of the city, returned to Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: They then evacuated the district of Baroda, retiring to the fortress of Dabhoi. On hearing of the death of Píláji, the viceroy immediately advanced against the Maráthás, and, after taking possession of Baroda, laid siege to Dabhoi.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____, Gujarát was wasted by famine
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1732, Gujarát was wasted by famine. Affairs at Surat, 1732.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Meanwhile, at Surat Múlla _____ of Athva was again the cause of disturbance
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Meanwhile, at Surat Múlla Muhammad Ali of Athva was again the cause of disturbance.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The messengers bearing these communications were intercepted at Broach by the partisans of _____, who determined to remove this powerful cause of anxiety
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Resisting with force the demand of a sum of 100,000 rupees by Sohráb Khán, the governor of Surat, he succeeded in driving Sohráb Khán out of the city, and the government of Surat was then usurped by Teghbeg Khán, a brother of Beglar-Beg Khán. The messengers bearing these communications were intercepted at Broach by the partisans of Teghbeg, who determined to remove this powerful cause of anxiety.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Teghbeg Khán, inviting Muhammad Ali to an entertainment, placed him in confinement, and after keeping him in prison for two years, in _____ put him to death
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Teghbeg Khán, inviting Muhammad Ali to an entertainment, placed him in confinement, and after keeping him in prison for two years, in 1734 put him to death.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Teghbeg also took possession of the fort of _____, and plundered it
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Teghbeg also took possession of the fort of Athva, and plundered it.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Sohráb Khán, seeing that he could not recover Surat, went with _____ to Ghogha, where his relatives lived, and from that, proceeding to Bhavnagar settled there
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Sohráb Khán, seeing that he could not recover Surat, went with Sayad Wali to Ghogha, where his relatives lived, and from that, proceeding to Bhavnagar settled there.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: When the emperor heard what had happened, he appointed Momín Khán to Surat and _____án to Cambay
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Teghbeg Khán, inviting Muhammad Ali to an entertainment, placed him in confinement, and after keeping him in prison for two years, in 1734 put him to death. When the emperor heard what had happened, he appointed Momín Khán to Surat and Teghbeg Khán to Cambay.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Momín Khán sent Sayad Núrullah to act for him, but he was defeated by Teghbeg Khán, who afterwards contrived, in _____, to be formally appointed governor of Surat with the title of Bahádur
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Momín Khán sent Sayad Núrullah to act for him, but he was defeated by Teghbeg Khán, who afterwards contrived, in 1733, to be formally appointed governor of Surat with the title of Bahádur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Collecting an army and taking with her Kántáji _____ and Dámáji Gáikwár, son of Píláji, she marched upon Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Collecting an army and taking with her Kántáji Kadam and Dámáji Gáikwár, son of Píláji, she marched upon Áhmedábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: For his services on this occasion Jawán _____án was made governor of Viramgam
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the end it was agreed that in addition to the one-fourth and the one-tenth shares of the revenue a sum of rupees 80,000 should be paid from the Áhmedábád treasury, Jawán Mard Khán being kept as a hostage till the payments were made. For his services on this occasion Jawán Mard Khán was made governor of Viramgam.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: During this year an imperial order appointed Khushálchand Sheth, son of _____, Nagar Sheth or chief merchant of Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: During this year an imperial order appointed Khushálchand Sheth, son of Shantidas Jhaveri, Nagar Sheth or chief merchant of Áhmedábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Umábái now marched upon _____, and the governor, Sher Khán Bábi, prepared to oppose the Maráthás
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Umábái now marched upon Baroda, and the governor, Sher Khán Bábi, prepared to oppose the Maráthás.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____, Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín Khán, governor of Junágaḍh died, and his son Mír Hazabr Khán was selected to fill his place
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1733, Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín Khán, governor of Junágaḍh died, and his son Mír Hazabr Khán was selected to fill his place.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Meanwhile, as the Maráthás had not received their rights, Jádoji Dábháde, son of Umábái, returned to _____át
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Meanwhile, as the Maráthás had not received their rights, Jádoji Dábháde, son of Umábái, returned to Gujarát.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Peace was concluded on the former basis, and Jádoji marched into _____ to exact tribute
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Peace was concluded on the former basis, and Jádoji marched into Sorath to exact tribute. In the meantime Sohráb Khán, the former governor of Surat, who had been kindly received by Bhávsinghji, the chief of Sihor, began to raise a following and was appointed collector of arrears in Sorath.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In the meantime Sohráb Khán, the former governor of Surat, who had been kindly received by Bhávsinghji, the chief of Sihor, began to raise a following and was appointed collector of arrears in _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Peace was concluded on the former basis, and Jádoji marched into Sorath to exact tribute. In the meantime Sohráb Khán, the former governor of Surat, who had been kindly received by Bhávsinghji, the chief of Sihor, began to raise a following and was appointed collector of arrears in Sorath.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In this year the _____ of the Chúnvál and Kánkrej committed many excesses, and a Rájput noble was robbed in the Pátan district
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In this year the Kolis of the Chúnvál and Kánkrej committed many excesses, and a Rájput noble was robbed in the Pátan district.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He chose _____ Núrullah as his deputy, and sent him to recover the revenue for the current year
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He chose Sayad Núrullah as his deputy, and sent him to recover the revenue for the current year.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At this time _____án Bábi was at Baroda, and his younger brother, though he resisted, was compelled to leave Ghogha
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: On the death of Salábat Khán Bábi, though the Mahárája had endeavoured to get Sher Khán Bábi appointed in place of his father, Ghogha had been granted to Burhán-ul-Mulk, who chose Sohráb Khán as his deputy. At this time Sher Khán Bábi was at Baroda, and his younger brother, though he resisted, was compelled to leave Ghogha.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The deputy governor of _____ complained to the governor of the oppressive conduct of Sohráb Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The deputy governor of Sorath complained to the governor of the oppressive conduct of Sohráb Khán. But Burhán-ul-Mulk supported Sohráb and having obtained for himself the government of Sorath, sent Sohráb Khán as his deputy to Junágaḍh.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____, Ratansingh Bhandári, the deputy viceroy, ordered Bhávsingh, son of Udaikaran, the hereditary officer of Víramgám, to be captured by Jawán-Mard Khán, imprisoned and sent him to Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1734, Ratansingh Bhandári, the deputy viceroy, ordered Bhávsingh, son of Udaikaran, the hereditary officer of Víramgám, to be captured by Jawán-Mard Khán, imprisoned and sent him to Áhmedábád. Baroda recovered by the Maráthás, 1734 In 1734, Sher Khán Bábi, governor of Baroda, went to visit his lands at Balasinor, leaving Muhammad Sarbáz in command at Baroda, Máhadáji Gáikwár, brother of Píláji, who then held Jambúsar, sending to Songad to Dámáji for aid, marched on Baroda with a strong force.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Jawan-_____án went so far as to arrest Bhávsingh, but was forced by his supporters to release him
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1734, Ratansingh Bhandári, the deputy viceroy, ordered Bhávsingh, son of Udaikaran, the hereditary officer of Víramgám, to be captured by Jawán-Mard Khán, imprisoned and sent him to Áhmedábád. Jawan-Mard Khán went so far as to arrest Bhávsingh, but was forced by his supporters to release him.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Momín Khán, who arrived after _____án's defeat, did not deem it prudent to engage the Maráthás, and retired to Cambay
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The garrison made a brave defence, and Sher Khán hearing of the attack at Bálásinor, called for aid from Ratansingh Bhandári, the deputy viceroy, who directed Momín Khán, the governor of Cambay, to join Sher Khán and drive back the Maráthás. Sher Khán started at once for Baroda.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In the meantime the garrison of Baroda, hopeless of succour, surrendered the town, and since that day Baroda continued to be the headquarters of the Gáikwár family until independence of India in _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the meantime the garrison of Baroda, hopeless of succour, surrendered the town, and since that day Baroda continued to be the headquarters of the Gáikwár family until independence of India in 1947.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At this time Dhanrúp Bhandári, governor of Petlád, died, and the farm of the districts of Nadiad, Arhar-Mátar, Petlád, and _____ was given to Momín Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: At this time Dhanrúp Bhandári, governor of Petlád, died, and the farm of the districts of Nadiad, Arhar-Mátar, Petlád, and Mahudha was given to Momín Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mulla Muhammad Áli managed to write letters from his confinement at Surat to the Nizám; and as that chief was now not far from Surat, he wrote urgently to _____án to release him
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mulla Muhammad Áli managed to write letters from his confinement at Surat to the Nizám; and as that chief was now not far from Surat, he wrote urgently to Teghbeg Khán to release him. Teghbeg Khán put the Mulla to death, and bribing the Nizám's messenger, gave out that he had died of joy at his release.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Khushálchand, the chief of the merchants of Áhmedábád, having had a difference with _____, was forced to leave the city, and sought shelter at Cambay and afterwards at Junágaḍh
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Khushálchand, the chief of the merchants of Áhmedábád, having had a difference with Ratansingh, was forced to leave the city, and sought shelter at Cambay and afterwards at Junágaḍh.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Jawán _____án conceived the design of conquering Idar from Anandsingh and Ráisingh, brothers of the Mahárája Abheysingh
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Jawán Mard Khán conceived the design of conquering Idar from Anandsingh and Ráisingh, brothers of the Mahárája Abheysingh. The Marátha chiefs at once marched to the help of Ídar, and Jawán Mard Khán, disbelieving the report of Marátha aid, continued to advance until he found himself opposed by an overwhelming force.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He accordingly marched upon Ídar, taking with him as allies Aghráji Koli of Katosan and _____ of Ilol Kánrah
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He accordingly marched upon Ídar, taking with him as allies Aghráji Koli of Katosan and Koli Amra of Ilol Kánrah.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In this strait _____ and Ráisingh sought the aid of Malhárráv Holkar and Ránoji Sindia, who were at this time in Málwa
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Jawán Mard Khán conceived the design of conquering Idar from Anandsingh and Ráisingh, brothers of the Mahárája Abheysingh. In this strait Anandsingh and Ráisingh sought the aid of Malhárráv Holkar and Ránoji Sindia, who were at this time in Málwa.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Negotiations were entered into, and Jawán _____án agreed to pay a sum of Rupees 1,75,000
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Marátha chiefs at once marched to the help of Ídar, and Jawán Mard Khán, disbelieving the report of Marátha aid, continued to advance until he found himself opposed by an overwhelming force. Negotiations were entered into, and Jawán Mard Khán agreed to pay a sum of Rupees 1,75,000.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Of the total amount _____ 25,000 were paid at once, and Zoráwar Khán, brother of Jawán Mard Khán, and Ajabsingh, agent of Aghráji Koli, were kept as hostages until the balance should be paid
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Negotiations were entered into, and Jawán Mard Khán agreed to pay a sum of Rupees 1,75,000. Of the total amount Rupees 25,000 were paid at once, and Zoráwar Khán, brother of Jawán Mard Khán, and Ajabsingh, agent of Aghráji Koli, were kept as hostages until the balance should be paid.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In this year _____án of Surat caused a wealthy merchant named Áhmed Chalabi to be assassinated, and confiscated his property
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In this year Teghbeg Khán of Surat caused a wealthy merchant named Áhmed Chalabi to be assassinated, and confiscated his property.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He also ordered _____ Áli to be put to death by certain Afgháns
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He also ordered Sayad Áli to be put to death by certain Afgháns.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Rivalry of Ratansingh Bhandári and Sohráb Khán, _____ In 1735, Dholka was assigned to Ratansingh Bhandári, and through the influence of Burhán-ul-Mulk, Sohráb Khán was appointed governor of Víramgám
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Rivalry of Ratansingh Bhandári and Sohráb Khán, 1735 In 1735, Dholka was assigned to Ratansingh Bhandári, and through the influence of Burhán-ul-Mulk, Sohráb Khán was appointed governor of Víramgám.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Ratansingh resented this, and eventually Víramgám was conferred on the Mahárája _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Ratansingh resented this, and eventually Víramgám was conferred on the Mahárája Abheysingh.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: When this order reached _____áb Khán, he forwarded it to Burhán-ul-Mulk, and in consequence of Burhán-ul-Mulk's remonstrances, the arrangements were changed and Sohráb Khán appointed governor
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Rivalry of Ratansingh Bhandári and Sohráb Khán, 1735 In 1735, Dholka was assigned to Ratansingh Bhandári, and through the influence of Burhán-ul-Mulk, Sohráb Khán was appointed governor of Víramgám. When this order reached Sohráb Khán, he forwarded it to Burhán-ul-Mulk, and in consequence of Burhán-ul-Mulk's remonstrances, the arrangements were changed and Sohráb Khán appointed governor.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: From Koth he advanced and pitched at _____, about ten miles from Sohráb Khán's camp, and here he was joined by Momín Khán and others whom he had summoned to support him
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: From Koth he advanced and pitched at Harala, about ten miles from Sohráb Khán's camp, and here he was joined by Momín Khán and others whom he had summoned to support him.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Defeat and Death of Sohráb Khán, _____ After the union of these forces he marched to Dholi, six miles from Dhandhuka, at which place Sohráb Khán was then encamped
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Defeat and Death of Sohráb Khán, 1735 After the union of these forces he marched to Dholi, six miles from Dhandhuka, at which place Sohráb Khán was then encamped.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: During the following night _____ári planned an attack on Sohráb Khán's camp
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Ratansingh Bhandári now proposed that peace should be concluded, and that Sohráb Khán should enjoy Víramgám until final orders were passed by the emperor. During the following night Ratansingh Bhandári planned an attack on Sohráb Khán's camp.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: By the death of Sohráb Khán the family of Kázím _____án became extinct
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: By the death of Sohráb Khán the family of Kázím Beg Khán became extinct.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He was buried at Sihor in _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He was buried at Sihor in Kathiwar.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Rivalry between Ratansingh Bhandári and Momín Khán, _____ After this success a single horseman attacked and wounded Ratansingh Bhandári in two places
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Rivalry between Ratansingh Bhandári and Momín Khán, 1735 After this success a single horseman attacked and wounded Ratansingh Bhandári in two places.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Ratansingh, who in two months had recovered from his injuries, now determined to attack Momín Khán, as that officer in the recent struggle had taken part with _____áb Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Ratansingh, who in two months had recovered from his injuries, now determined to attack Momín Khán, as that officer in the recent struggle had taken part with Sohráb Khán. Kaliánchand, was appointed to Víramgám in place of Sher Khán Bábi, and instead of Sohráb Khán, Muhsin Khán Khálvi was made deputy governor of Sorath.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Momín Khán hearing of _____'s intentions, withdrew to Cambay
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Rivalry between Ratansingh Bhandári and Momín Khán, 1735 After this success a single horseman attacked and wounded Ratansingh Bhandári in two places. Ratansingh, who in two months had recovered from his injuries, now determined to attack Momín Khán, as that officer in the recent struggle had taken part with Sohráb Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In the course of this year, on the expiry of the period of the farm of _____, Arhar-Mátar, and Naḍiád, these districts were transferred from Momín Khán to Safdar Khán Bábi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the course of this year, on the expiry of the period of the farm of Mahudha, Arhar-Mátar, and Naḍiád, these districts were transferred from Momín Khán to Safdar Khán Bábi.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Kaliánchand, was appointed to Víramgám in place of _____án Bábi, and instead of Sohráb Khán, Muhsin Khán Khálvi was made deputy governor of Sorath
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Kaliánchand, was appointed to Víramgám in place of Sher Khán Bábi, and instead of Sohráb Khán, Muhsin Khán Khálvi was made deputy governor of Sorath.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Battle of Ánand-Mogri, _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Battle of Ánand-Mogri, 1735.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time Dámáji Gáikwár, who had been chosen by Umábái as her representative in Gujarát, appointed _____ to act as his agent
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Dámáji Gáikwár, who had been chosen by Umábái as her representative in Gujarát, appointed Rangoji to act as his agent. Rangoji met him, and a battle was fought at Ánand-Mogri, twenty-five miles south-east of Kheda, in which Kántáji was defeated and his son killed.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Kántáji being dissatisfied with this arrangement, in which his rights were ignored, marched into _____át
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Dámáji Gáikwár, who had been chosen by Umábái as her representative in Gujarát, appointed Rangoji to act as his agent. Kántáji being dissatisfied with this arrangement, in which his rights were ignored, marched into Gujarát.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Rangoji met him, and a battle was fought at Ánand-_____, twenty-five miles south-east of Kheda, in which Kántáji was defeated and his son killed
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Battle of Ánand-Mogri, 1735. Rangoji met him, and a battle was fought at Ánand-Mogri, twenty-five miles south-east of Kheda, in which Kántáji was defeated and his son killed.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In consequence of this reverse Kántáji retired to _____ád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In consequence of this reverse Kántáji retired to Petlád. Momín Khán, who with his army was drawn up near Petlád to oppose Rangoji, was compelled to retire to Cambay, where peace was concluded on condition that Dámáji should receive the one-fourth share of the revenues of the country north of the Mahi.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As the districts where these battles were fought were held in farm by _____án Bábi, he suffered much loss, and consequently retired to Rádhanpur
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: As the districts where these battles were fought were held in farm by Safdar Khán Bábi, he suffered much loss, and consequently retired to Rádhanpur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Rangoji was joined by Dámáji Gáikwár, and these two leaders went together to _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Rangoji was joined by Dámáji Gáikwár, and these two leaders went together to Dholka.
